newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britons jailed in Cyprus for patents burglary.
newsitem.headline: Britons jailed in Cyprus for patents burglary.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Wednesday jailed two British private detectives for 18 months for burglary and stealing documents related to the island's pharmaceuticals industry.
Paul Whybrow, 47, and Michael Flack, 52, from Bexley, southeast of London, pleaded guilty to the single burglary charge at a criminal court in the southern port town of Limassol.
They confessed to stealing documents from a customs clearing office in February relating to the imports of raw materials by a local pharmaceuticals firm.
Defence lawyers said the accused were investigating the unlawful copying of patented products on an international scale, with emphasis on pharmaceuticals, the judge said in summing up the case.

"Undoubtedly the intention was the financial interests of their clients... adopting illegal means to further possible legal purposes, if that was finally going to be proven. But their actions were unacceptable," he said.
The two men were arrested hours after the break-in on the steps of an aeroplane ready to leave for London.
Their defence lawyer says a third person, a Cypriot who urged the two to commit the crime, is still at large.
"It was a definite set-up. One hundred percent," Whylbrow told journalists.
Cyprus has a burgeoning pharmaceuticals industry and some local companies manufacture drugs under licence from multinational corporations.
